root: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures?
gaps: No published pose-depth (model-count) scaling study for AAV capsid–receptor complexes exists; the closest comparators are 10 AF-Multimer models per competition (Ding et al. 2024) and 5 models with up to 20 recycles for LRP6 complexes (Shay et al. 2024), so the card's 144–2,880 arms have no prior baseline beyond the ten-model published one.

Per-pair transcytose-versus-retain phenotype labels are scarce: Voyager's MDCK Transwell result covers VCAP-102±ALPL vs AAV9 only, and most programs (Dyno, Capsida, Gradinaru) score in vivo brain transduction rather than transcytosis rate, so the card's training labels may rest on few direct measurements.

APPRAISE-style modeling uses isolated VR-VIII peptides (AA587–594), not the full 60-mer capsid at the 3-fold spike with GPI anchor and membrane; a 'shared 3-fold motif' may partly reflect the peptide-competition setup, and weak avidity-dependent contacts can evade prediction (the card's own caveat).

Species gaps limit motif generality: LY6A/LY6C1 are mouse-restricted (absent in primates), 9P31/9P36 bind mouse but not primate CA4, while ALPL is conserved — a motif validated on mouse GPI receptors may not transfer to human-relevant pairs.

Dyno's and Capsida's structural pipelines are proprietary, so 'already done' cannot be settled for them; Capsida's NR001–NR005 human BBB-receptor platform with plate-/bead-based capsid/receptor binding assays (capsida.com) and Lir's Starfish capsid-structure/docking pipeline (lirtx.com) are additional consumers of this result that were not assessed in depth here.

programmes.name: Voyager Therapeutics — TRACER capsid discovery and ALPL NeuroShuttle (VCAP-102 / VY1706)
programmes.step: Mechanism-of-action step of the TRACER pipeline the card targets: after RNA-guided in vivo capsid evolution, Voyager identifies the vascular receptor each capsid uses to cross the BBB and demonstrates that binding of that receptor initiates transcytosis rather than mere uptake — i.e., the transcytose-versus-retain call per capsid–receptor pair. In practice this is done with human surface-protein binding/transduction screens, SPR, and a polarized cell-barrier Transwell assay, not with exhaustive structural enumeration.

activity.claim: Active as of 2026: the lead program VY1706 is a TRACER-derived capsid gene therapy with AAIC 2026 NHP GLP toxicology data and dosing in early Alzheimer's disease expected in Q4 2026; ALPL-VYGR-NeuroShuttle sits in the wholly-owned research pipeline.

claims.claim: Scale of the discovery funnel feeding the receptor step: TRACER-NHP libraries start at ~4E7 individual capsid variants, narrowed by two in vivo macaque passages to ~1,500 variants of interest before receptor work.
Receptor identification is done experimentally with two orthogonal screens (human surface-protein binding microarray and ORFeome transduction screen), not by complex modeling.
The transcytose-versus-retain call is made in a polarized cell-barrier (MDCK Transwell) model: human ALPL expression raises VCAP-102 transcytosis >100-fold while AAV9 is unaffected.

Voyager already works with predicted capsid–receptor interface residues and treats cross-species conservation of the contact set as its translatability argument, so interface-signature outputs are directly consumable.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If exhaustive pose enumeration shows that transcytosis-competent pairs share a 3-fold-axis GPI-anchor engagement geometry (competent-minus-retained gap ≥0.50 at 2,880 models), Voyager gains a structural signature for ALPL-engaging capsids — including the VCAP-102 SPH-family insert at VR-IV on the 3-fold spike — that can gate TRACER hits and Gen2 capsids before SPR/Transwell/NHP work, prioritize variants predicted to trigger transcytosis rather than intracellular retention, and inform ALPL-NeuroShuttle binder design; the mechanism story behind VY1706 and partnered programs would gain a predictive interface biomarker.
programmes.if_not_changes: If deeper pose sampling leaves the gap within 0.15 of its 144-model value (insert location already fixes the 3-fold engagement site), nothing changes: Voyager keeps receptor ID via cell-microarray/ORFeome screens and the MDCK Transwell transcytosis model, and capsid–receptor complex enumeration would not enter its Go/No-Go decisions.

already_done.claim: Voyager has run the closest analogue — receptor ID plus a cell-barrier transcytosis demonstration for one capsid family (VCAP-102/ALPL), SPR affinity, cryo-EM showing the insert at the 3-fold apex, and predicted capsid–ALPL contact residues — but has not published exhaustive pose-depth sampling across a capsid panel with transcytose-versus-retain labels.

programmes.name: Gradinaru Lab (Caltech) / APPRAISE-AAV — receptor-directed AAV engineering and the open-source APPRAISE package
programmes.step: The computational step the card scales: ranking engineered capsid insertion peptides against BBB receptors by AlphaFold-Multimer pairwise competition modeling, scored with atom-counting energy plus binding-angle and pocket-depth geometry, used to classify receptor-dependent vs receptor-independent capsids and to pick candidates before in vivo selection. Today this runs at ten models per competition on single-GPU Colab sessions; the card asks whether 144–2,880 pose models per pair change the transcytosis call.

activity.claim: Active: the APPRAISE repository received commits on Apr 9, 2026 (1.3.0 package and Boltz-1/Chai-1/OpenFold3 compatibility), and the lab published human CA-IV-targeted capsid AAV-hCA4-IV77 in Cell Reports on Oct 31, 2025.

claims.claim: Standard depth of pose sampling is ten AF-Multimer models per pairwise competition (five predictions per input order, two orders), averaged into a round-robin ranking matrix.
Scale and cost of the step today: a 100-capsid HT-APPRAISE screen completed in 24 h on three parallel Colab GPU sessions, with ~0.1–1 GPU minute per peptide–receptor model and sub-second CPU scoring.
Applied to LY6A, LY6C1 and CA4, the 10-model ranking recovered validated binders but produced documented false negatives — the exact failure mode deeper pose sampling is meant to fix.

Where full complex modeling has been run (LRP6–capsid VR-VIII), the lab used only five AF-Multimer models with up to 20 recycles on a single A100, and validated poses experimentally and on macaque/human primary brain microvascular endothelial cells.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If the competent-minus-retained engagement gap grows to ≥0.50 only at 2,880 models, the lab would raise APPRAISE's default replicate depth (and could add rigid-docking poses), and a shared 3-fold GPI-anchor motif would become an explicit interface feature alongside its angle/depth geometry terms — letting it triage capsid–receptor pairs and rescue false negatives (e.g., 9P08–LY6A, 9P36–CA4) before humanized-mouse selections for PHP.eC- and hCA4-type vectors.
programmes.if_not_changes: If the gap stays within 0.15 of the 144-model value, nothing changes: the lab keeps ten-model pairwise competitions and its assumption that insert location (VR-VIII AA587–594 at the 3-fold spike) already fixes the engagement site, and the deeper enumeration compute is not justified.

already_done.claim: This lab produced the closest prior work: APPRAISE matrices at ten AF-Multimer models per competition across LY6A/LY6C1/CA4 pairings, a validated PHP.eB–LY6A pose used as the reference anchor, five-model LRP6 complex models with cryo-ET, and observed false negatives — but it has not run pose-depth sweeps (144–2,880) or tested a shared 3-fold GPI motif against transcytosis-versus-retention phenotype labels.

programmes.name: Dyno Therapeutics — multi-mechanism BBB-crossing capsid portfolio (ALPL, TfR1, Dyno-discovered receptors)
programmes.step: The step the card targets is Dyno's mechanism assignment and structure-aware design for its CNS portfolio: deciding which BBB receptor each engineered capsid engages and whether that engagement crosses the BBB, then engineering capsids for several BBB-crossing mechanisms in parallel (ALPL, hTfR1, and Dyno-discovered receptors) rather than one pathway. Dyno states it integrates sequence- and structure-based approaches in its generative design, with receptor mechanism confirmed by head-to-head in vivo comparisons.

activity.claim: Active: Dyno launched the ALPL-targeting Dyno-9zh capsid in 2026 and the TfR1-targeting Dyno-yp2 on Jan 12, 2026, with further capsid launches at ASGCT 2026, and runs active Roche/Novartis/Sarepta/Astellas partnerships.

claims.claim: Dyno deliberately portfolios multiple BBB-crossing mechanisms and treats receptor mechanism as a translatability lever, so a cross-capsid binding signature for transcytosis would sit directly on its decision path.
Its ALPL mechanism (the same GPI-anchored receptor class as the card's motif hypothesis) is validated phenotypically by head-to-head in vivo comparisons of ALPL-targeting capsids in mouse and NHP.

Scale of the experimental funnel that any in silico signature would filter: LEAP with billions of in vivo sequence–function measurements per month, aimed at CNS partners such as Roche ($50M upfront, Oct 2024).

programmes.if_lever_changes: If exhaustive enumeration yields a shared 3-fold GPI-engagement signature separating transcytosing from retained pairs (and the gap only appears at high model counts), Dyno could adopt the signature as a design/filter feature in its sequence+structure generative pipeline for ALPL and its discovered-receptor capsids, rank generated capsids by predicted transcytosis-competent geometry to cut in vivo screening, and strengthen the receptor-mechanism translation package its Roche/Novartis partners need.
programmes.if_not_changes: If pose depth does not change the call, Dyno's practice is unchanged: capsid selection remains driven by in vivo phenotype at LEAP scale plus receptor-engagement validation, and capsid–receptor complex enumeration would not affect which mechanisms or capsids it advances.

already_done.claim: No public record shows Dyno has run exhaustive capsid–receptor pose enumeration: its published practice validates receptor mechanisms in vivo (head-to-head ALPL-targeting capsids in mouse and NHP) and folds structure-based approaches into generative design, but any pose-depth studies remain proprietary and unverifiable.
